scope: Metadata, selected experimental claims, database evidence codes, and reuse terms supporting the citrus/lavender comparison.
limits: Focused narrative audit; no comprehensive literature review, independent experiment, full ML reproduction, or reprocessing of raw structural/assay data.

supported_claims: The study classifies monoterpene synthases using AlphaFold2-derived, manually selected Fpocket active-site features.
The curated class labels derive from published GC-MS profiles, with at least 70% of products in the linear or cyclic class.
The paper reports 88 curated sequences, a modelling dataset of 87 observations, and explicit performance-related exclusions.
limitations: This project does not reproduce the paper's model training or reported accuracy.
The paper's methods exclude A0A8H4VHP2 and O22340 because inclusion reduced model performance; this selection history limits interpretation of performance.
The paper contains model-dependent and exploratory interpretations, not universal causal rules for cyclisation.
Full body retrieved; relevant methods, results, interpretation and data availability inspected. Supplementary experiments and every cited source were not independently re-audited.
corrections: Use the published title, not the different title wording in the repository's README citation.
references.rights: Article CC BY 3.0; software/data repository has separate MIT notice.
references.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.

supported_claims: Selected Citrus sinensis enzyme converts GPP primarily to (+)-limonene under the reported assay.
GC-MS reports 99% limonene, 0.7% beta-myrcene and 0.3% alpha-pinene; enantiomer assignment is supported by circular dichroism comparison.
The crystal represents an apo/open conformation at 2.3 angstrom resolution; the experimental expression construct removes residues 1–52 and adds an affinity tag.
limitations: Full body retrieved and relevant construct, product, structure and interpretation sections inspected; original raw chromatograms and diffraction data were not reprocessed.
Reported catalytic constants depend on assay conditions and cofactors, so they are not a matched comparison with lavender.
The primary publication does not establish that every sequence annotation in the current database record was directly measured.
corrections: The ATC cyclic-class fraction 99.3% includes 0.3% alpha-pinene and must not be presented as the limonene fraction.
Do not equate the full 607-residue sequence with the experimentally expressed construct or coordinate coverage.
references.rights: PMC permits text-mining retrieval; no general open reuse license returned. Cite/link; do not redistribute the article.
references.title: Functional and Structural Characterization of a (+)-Limonene Synthase from Citrus sinensis.

supported_claims: The primary abstract reports that lavender LaLINS produces exclusively (R)-(−)-linalool in its characterization.
LaLIMS is a separate, multiproduct enzyme in the same paper and must not be confused with LaLINS.
limitations: Only PubMed metadata and abstract were inspected; primary full text and detailed assay conditions were not read.
Detailed lavender assay context in ATC is secondary curation, not an independently verified transcription here.
Exclusive product formation is a report for the studied assay, not a claim about every substrate or condition.
references.rights: No PMCID or explicit open reuse license returned; cite/link to the publication.
references.title: Cloning and functional characterization of three terpene synthases from lavender (Lavandula angustifolia).

supported_claims: A primary experimental structure was reported for Mentha spicata (4S)-limonene synthase with fluorinated substrate/intermediate analogues.
This provides a historical structural reference for the family, distinct from the selected Citrus sinensis enzyme.
limitations: Only abstract and metadata inspected; automated full-text requests failed, and the rights response did not permit full-text retrieval.
The existence of a related limonene structure does not supply experimental coordinates for the selected lavender enzyme.
references.rights: Copyright National Academy of Sciences; no permissive license returned.
references.title: Structure of limonene synthase, a simple model for terpenoid cyclase catalysis.
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

supported_claims: Alanine-scanning and enzyme-fidelity experiments in spearmint limonene synthase identified effects of W324/H579 mutations on activity and product profile.
These experiments support treating specificity as dependent on residue context rather than one universal motif.
limitations: Only abstract and metadata inspected; full-text retrieval failed and the rights response did not permit automated full text.
Mutations in spearmint cannot be assumed to have the same effect at apparently corresponding positions in citrus or lavender.
references.title: Functional analysis of (4S)-limonene synthase mutants reveals determinants of catalytic outcome in a model monoterpene synthase.
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

supported_claims: Bacterial bLinS from Streptomyces clavuligerus makes R-linalool from GPP and trans-nerolidol from FPP in the reported assays.
The authors identify the FGPP pose in one bLinS monomer as noncatalytic and discuss incomplete metal binding and crystal packing.
Bacterial and plant monoterpene synthases differ in domain architecture; the bacterial example is not the selected lavender enzyme.
limitations: Full body retrieved in two pages; relevant product, structural interpretation and conclusion sections inspected.
This is background evidence, not the primary evidence for Q2XSC5 or an experimental structure of lavender LaLINS.
No production-titer or mechanistic claim is extrapolated to the selected enzymes.
references.rights: CC BY statement in PMC; retain author/source attribution.
references.title: Structural Basis of Catalysis in the Bacterial Monoterpene Synthases Linalool Synthase and 1,8-Cineole Synthase.

supported_claims: Mentha citrata linalool synthase was cloned and characterized as a distinct R-linalool synthase.
The paper illustrates species-specific enzyme characterization; it is not a study of lavender LaLINS.
limitations: Only abstract and metadata inspected; no PMCID returned.
Homology-model discussion is not experimental structure evidence for the selected lavender enzyme.
references.rights: No explicit open reuse license returned; cite/link.
references.title: Molecular cloning and characterization of a new linalool synthase.
ATC / Pockets to Products repository
supported_claims: CharacterisedSeqRef.csv has 88 enzyme records with class fractions, sequences, assay contexts and primary citations.
FullDataset.csv has 87 rows: 59 linear and 28 cyclic, with derived active-site features.
Both selected accessions occur in the reference and feature tables.
The repository README and LICENSE identify MIT terms, copyright 2025 Cathal Ó Raghallaigh.
limitations: The repository is a versioned secondary curation and derived-feature source, not a new assay performed here.
A cyclic or linear class fraction is not necessarily the named product fraction.
Its README uses different paper-title wording; cite the verified published title.
The article's CC BY license and the repository MIT notice apply to different materials; upstream database rights remain separate.
corrections: Preserve cyclic 99.3% versus limonene 99% for the citrus example.
references.rights: MIT notice inspected; preserve copyright and license with copied material.

limitations: Sequence annotation and experimental construct are different records.
Chloroplast location is a sequence-based annotation (ECO:0000255); reviewed status does not make every field an experimental observation.

references.title: UniProtKB Q2XSC5
supported_claims: Pinned reviewed protein record contains a 564-residue sequence and field-specific evidence annotations.
limitations: Function and catalytic-reaction annotations cite experimental evidence (ECO:0000269) from Landmann2007.
Cofactor and three-metal-ion statements use evidence by similarity (ECO:0000250), not direct experimental evidence in this annotation.
A reviewed sequence record is not an experimental structure.
references.rights: CC BY 4.0; see source manifest and https://www.uniprot.org/help/license

references.title: PDB 5UV0: Citrus sinensis (+)-limonene synthase
supported_claims: RCSB metadata links 5UV0 to Morehouse2017 and reports an X-ray structure at 2.3 angstrom resolution.
Entry metadata records 522 modeled polymer residues and 607 deposited polymer positions; no nonpolymer entity is deposited.
The archived A245/V245 conflict annotation is not a difference between the pinned current UniProt and deposited polymer sequences: both have A245 and all 607 positions match.
limitations: The sequence record, expressed construct, deposited polymer sequence and modeled coordinates must be distinguished.
An apo structure does not show bound native substrate, product, or the reaction in motion.
This record supplies experimental structure evidence for citrus, not for the selected lavender enzyme.
The archival sequence-discrepancy annotation refers to an earlier reference; no engineered mutation is recorded.
references.rights: wwPDB archive data CC0; retain primary citation and any separately attributed annotations.
